title: Help Olivia Fight Her Brain Tumour
description: Olivia, 21, has been diagnosed with a grade IV glioblastoma (GBM) — the most aggressive malignant brain tumour. She urgently needs dendritic cell immunotherapy in Germany — a treatment that is not covered by OHIP or any public health system.

story.intro: Olivia is a 21-year-old medical student at the University of Toronto who was diagnosed with Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM), WHO grade IV — the most aggressive malignant brain tumour. Standard treatment (surgery, radiotherapy, temozolomide) offers a median survival of just 14-16 months. The only therapy that could significantly extend her survival — dendritic cell immunotherapy — is available only at specialised centres in Germany and is not covered by OHIP or any public health system.

sections.title: The Diagnosis
sections.content:
It all started in October 2025, when Olivia began experiencing persistent morning headaches accompanied by nausea and blurred vision in her left eye. On 20th October, after a seizure during a lecture at the Temerty Faculty of Medicine at the University of Toronto, she was rushed to the Krembil Brain Institute at Toronto Western Hospital.

The MRI revealed a 4.2 cm mass in her right frontal lobe with characteristic ring enhancement and perilesional oedema. Stereotactic biopsy and molecular analysis confirmed the diagnosis: Glioblastoma Multiforme, IDH-wildtype, WHO grade IV, with unmethylated MGMT promoter — the most unfavourable molecular subtype, meaning reduced response to chemotherapy.

sections.title: Standard Treatment and Its Limits
sections.content:
Olivia underwent partial surgical resection (subtotal resection) on 15th November 2025 at Toronto Western Hospital — complete removal was not possible due to the tumour's proximity to functional speech areas. She then followed the Stupp protocol: concurrent radiotherapy (30 sessions over 6 weeks) with daily temozolomide, followed by maintenance cycles of temozolomide.

Her doctors were honest: with unmethylated MGMT, response to temozolomide is expected to be limited. Median survival with standard treatment is 12-15 months. The follow-up MRI in September 2026 showed residual tumour stable in size, but her doctors warned that recurrence is almost certain.

sections.title: The Hope: Dendritic Cell Immunotherapy
sections.content:
After extensive research, Olivia's family identified a specialised dendritic cell immunotherapy programme at a certified oncology centre in Germany. A recent clinical study (Human Vaccines & Immunotherapeutics, 2025) demonstrated a 68% increase in median overall survival for glioblastoma patients who received dendritic cell vaccines.

The therapy works as follows: cells are harvested from Olivia's blood, converted into dendritic cells in the laboratory, 'trained' with antigens from her own tumour, and reinfused to activate her immune system against the cancer. 4-6 cycles are required over 12 months.

This therapy is NOT covered by OHIP and has not been approved by Health Canada. It is classified as 'innovative therapy' and is available only on a private-pay basis at specialised centres in Germany.

sections.title: Why We Need Your Help
sections.content: We want to be completely transparent. Olivia's standard treatment — surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy — was provided free of charge by Ontario's public health plan (OHIP) at Toronto Western Hospital. That is covered. What is NOT covered by OHIP, or by any public health system, is dendritic cell immunotherapy in Germany — a treatment that clinical studies show can increase survival by 68%. We need $135,000 to give Olivia a real chance at life beyond the 14-month standard prognosis.

quote.text: I wanted to become a doctor to help people. Now I'm learning what it means to be a patient — and how unbearable it is to know that a treatment exists that could save you, but you can't access it. Every donation isn't just money — it's time. Time I get to keep living. If I make it through this, I promise to dedicate my life to neuro-oncology, so no one else has to go through what I'm going through.
quote.author: Olivia M.

updates.title: Follow-up MRI results are in 📋
updates.content: The follow-up MRI after completing radiotherapy shows stable residual tumour with no new lesions. Her doctors at Toronto Western Hospital say this is the best possible outcome with standard treatment, but recurrence remains very likely. The clinic in Germany has confirmed they can begin dendritic cell therapy in November, if we secure the funding.

updates.title: We've passed 1,000 donors! 🙏
updates.content: Your support has been overwhelming — more than 1,000 people have given. Olivia has finished her maintenance temozolomide cycles and is feeling strong. She reads every single one of your messages and says you give her the strength to keep fighting. Every dollar brings us closer to Germany.

updates.title: Treatment update
updates.content: Olivia has completed concurrent chemoradiation at Toronto Western Hospital. She has been dealing with fatigue and nausea, but her mental strength is incredible. Her neuro-oncologist explained that with unmethylated MGMT, temozolomide alone isn't enough — which is why immunotherapy is critical.

updates.title: The campaign has launched
updates.content: With heavy hearts but determination, we're launching this appeal. After months of intensive treatment in the public system, her doctors told us clearly: standard treatment buys time, but immunotherapy can give her a life. Unfortunately, it isn't covered by OHIP. We believe in the power of community.
